If you haven't heard, this is about Puttitout's [announcement](https://voat.co/v/announcements/1415644) from the other day. While the prospect of less spam is very welcome, this move has the potential for a massive fuck up.

Voat has always been anti-mod, or at least has a negative view of mods. There has always been a certain degree of scrutiny placed on mods, particularly those who mod defaults. They are held to a higher standard than the rest, and rightly so. However, Voat's plan seems to be that they will be taking on 3-5 janitor mods in each default. That's a lot. It is just common sense that there will be a handful of 'bad eggs' in there. Some of these will be appointed, and they will be threat to the system subs. Yes, they don't have much power. They can only remove posts. But what happens if there is more than one rogue janitor, what if there are 3 or 4. A systematic, coordinated attack on a sub can do massive damage. Some of the defaults only have 2-3 mods, some only have 1 or no mods active on Voat. An attack on such a sub could ruin it. If there are no mods active, then we are waiting for Admin intervention. We know how long that usually takes, by then a sub can be irreparably damaged.

Since the announcement, there has been a massive influx of janitor requests in v/subverserequests. The vast majority are regular Voat users, who want to help out. However, there are a few users making applications who look a bit sketchy. (This is *not* an attack on this user, it is just an example). The user Stradian has made requests for v/news, v/technology and v/programming, some of the biggest subs on the site. He has been a user for 1.5 years and has only made 15 submissions. 2 in news, 1 in technology and 0 in programming. Why would someone who hardly contributes to these subs want to moderate them? The user has made most of his submissions to v/niggers, so it's fair to say he has a strong political opinion (not an attack on the sub). Maybe this user wants to mod news so they can delete posts they don't agree with politically. Maybe this account is an alt who posted to v/niggers for the easy ccp/scp. What I'm trying to say is that this gives power to users who wouldn't and shouldn't usually ever get any, especially in defaults. This guy won't be accepted, you have to fulfill the activity restrictions of a normal subverse request. But what happens when someone with ulterior motives has a more fleshed out alt. They get the role and they can spread their influence.

If I were the one of the admins, I'd reconsider what the requirements are. The user should have more than just 2 submissions and 2 comments. They should be a regular poster and trusted user. The current full mods should be actively consulted during this period, as we saw with v/videos the definition of spam isn't set in stone. Either the janitors need to be on board with that subs definition of spam, or there needs to be an unambiguous definition of spam for all default subs. I believe 3-5 is far too many new mods. Quality modding is a lot better than a high quantity of mods, especially with Voat's attitude to moderation. Some some subs such as v/gaming have stated that they don't need any janitor mods as they have spam under control. This should be considered on an individual sub basis. I don't think throwing more mods at a problem is a particularly effective method. Another way to improve the quality of modding us to get rid of inactive moderators. There are far too many default mods that don't contribute to their sub, whether it's submissions or comments, or are inactive on Voat altogether. A lot of spam gets through on defaults because the mods are inactive. These need to be replaced with trusted mods who are passionate about the sub.

You may think this is paranoid or an overreaction, but certain groups don't need any help in taking control of subs. This is just handing it to them on a silver platter. So I ask the admins to reconsider their requirements and to make your selections with care and I ask Voat users to stay vigilant.
